title: MUS and MSS enumeration (MARCO)
description: All minimal unsatisfiable subsets (MUSes) and maximal satisfiable subsets (MSSes) of a CNF formula, with the MARCO loop: a map solver proposes unexplored seeds, the check says whether a seed is satisfiable, and the seed is grown or shrunk by walking the assumption list (a.true, E.flip(a)). Both outcomes refine the map, in opposite directions (G.below, G.above). The MUSes are the solutions; the MSSes are a second kind of solution (accept ... as mss), listed in Messages and counted next to Solutions and in the Statistics tab. Counts checked by brute force over all subsets.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The instance (Instances tab): pos(C,V) and neg(C,V) are the literals of clause C.
cl(C) :- pos(C,_).
cl(C) :- neg(C,_).
var(V) :- pos(_,V).
var(V) :- neg(_,V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% The map: a seed is any set of clauses (pick/1) not yet explored. Grown seeds (MSSes) block
% their subsets, shrunk seeds (MUSes) block their supersets; the map learns only these clauses.
{ pick(C) : cl(C) }.
% Maximal seeds first (Liffiton and Malik's getUnexploredMax): with --heuristic=Domain the
% solver decides every pick to true first.
#heuristic pick(C) : cl(C). [1,true]
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Is the seed satisfiable? An assignment that satisfies every picked clause.
{ t(V) } :- var(V).
sat(C) :- pos(C,V), t(V).
sat(C) :- neg(C,V), not t(V).
:- pick(C), not sat(C).
#show t/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction    options "--heuristic=Domain"
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# MARCO (Liffiton, Previti, Malik and Marques-Silva): every seed is explored. A satisfiable seed
# grows to a maximal satisfiable subset (MSS): add clauses while the check still succeeds. An
# unsatisfiable one shrinks to a minimal unsatisfiable subset (MUS): drop clauses while the
# check still fails. Both kinds are reported, and both refine the map: G.below(E) removes the
# MSS and its subsets, G.above(E) the MUS and its supersets. The MUSes are the solutions; the
# MSSes are a second kind (accept ... as mss), listed and counted apart. The run ends when the
# map has no seed left.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    E = G(M)
    if C.solve(assume E):
        for a in E:
            if not a.true and C.solve(assume E.flip(a)): E = E.flip(a)
        accept A.solve(assume E) as mss
        A.add(G.below(E))
    else:
        for a in E:
            if a.true and not C.solve(assume E.flip(a)): E = E.flip(a)
        accept A.solve(assume E)
        A.add(G.above(E))

generators.name: random-cnf
generators.description: A random CNF: c clauses over the variables 1..v, each with 1 to k literals.
generators.text:
% random-cnf: c clauses over the variables 1..v; clause C has 1 to k literals (uniform), each
% on a uniform variable with a sign of probability 1/2 (a repeated literal counts once).
clause(1..c).
len(C,@int(1, k, C, len)) :- clause(C).
lit(C,J,@int(1, v, C, J)) :- len(C,N), J = 1..N.
pos(C,V) :- lit(C,J,V), @flip(500, C, J, sign) = 1.
neg(C,V) :- lit(C,J,V), @flip(500, C, J, sign) = 0.
#show pos/2.
#show neg/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction    options "--heuristic=Domain"
solver C = shared + check
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# MARCO without growing: a satisfiable seed blocks only itself and its subsets (no MSS is
# reported); unsatisfiable seeds still shrink to MUSes.
loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    E = G(M)
    if C.solve(assume E):
        A.add(G.below(E))
    else:
        for a in E:
            if a.true and not C.solve(assume E.flip(a)): E = E.flip(a)
        accept A.solve(assume E)
        A.add(G.above(E))

library.summary: MARCO: every MUS (the solutions) and MSS (logged) of a CNF formula, by growing and shrinking seeds of a map solver (10 clauses, 7 MUSes, 12 MSSes).
